name: Acute myeloblastic leukemia without maturation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues

criteria.description: Presence of ≥20% myeloblasts in bone marrow or peripheral blood
Myeloblasts without significant maturation beyond the promyelocyte stage
Expression of myeloid markers such as CD13, CD33, and MPO positivity on blasts
Absence of recurrent genetic abnormalities defining other AML subtypes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: ≥20% myeloblasts in bone marrow or blood with absence of maturation beyond myeloblast stage
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other AML subtypes with specific genetic abnormalities.

searchTerms: increased immature white blood cells in blood

pathognomonic.notes: Resulting in anemia, thrombocytopenia, and neutropenia
searchTerms: bone marrow not producing enough blood cells
failure to make red, white cells and platelets

common.symptomName: Anemia-related pallor and dyspnea on exertion
common.notes: Due to decreased red blood cell production
searchTerms: pale skin and shortness of breath

common.notes: Increased susceptibility to bacterial and fungal infections
searchTerms: recurrent infections due to immune weakness
infections caused by low white blood cells

common.symptomName: Petechiae and mucosal bleeding from thrombocytopenia
searchTerms: small red spots and bleeding from low platelets

common.notes: Often due to leukemic cytokine release
searchTerms: temperature rise with no infection found

occasional.notes: Enlargement of liver and spleen due to leukemic infiltration
Enlarged lymph nodes from leukemic infiltration

searchTerms: losing weight and sweating at night

rare.symptomName: Central nervous system involvement with neurological deficits
rare.notes: Leukemic infiltration causing cranial nerve palsies or seizures
searchTerms: nerve deficits due to CNS involvement

rare.symptomName: Chloroma (myeloid sarcoma) presenting as extramedullary mass

laboratory: Bone marrow biopsy with predominant myeloblasts lacking maturation
imaging: Chest X-ray to evaluate for infection or leukemic infiltrates
CT scan for detection of extramedullary masses (chloromas)
other: Immunophenotyping confirming myeloid lineage markers (CD13, CD33, MPO)
Coagulation studies to assess for disseminated intravascular coagulation

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of myeloblasts with evidence of maturation beyond promyelocyte stage
Lymphoid rather than myeloid lineage markers

redFlags: Signs of bleeding or bruising without trauma
references: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues, 2016
Orphanet: Acute myeloblastic leukemia without maturation (ORPHA:98833)
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 20th Edition, Chapter on Acute Myeloid Leukemia
